battle.name: 隋擊突厥之戰
battle.theater: 靈州朔州與河套陰山邊塞
battle.brief: 開皇十九年正月，隋軍分六路發兵三十萬，攻突厥於靈州朔州與河套陰山。前年冬楊素夜襲達頭可汗牙營得手，達頭兵敗被部下所殺，十餘萬降隋；開皇二十年再出，頗利可汗大潰奔鐵山。卡面羅馬標槍不在此役現場，但它破盾逼敵退回掩體的辦法，正是隋軍用弩齊射破衝鋒的邏輯。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 開皇十九年至二十年的隋朝與突厥之戰，交戰方是北方的隋朝與漠北的東突厥汗國，第三方則是正在自相攻殺的突厥可汗們。隋朝這邊，開皇十九年（599）在位的是隋文帝楊堅，滅陳已過十年，開皇年號行至第十九年。軍隊骨幹是府兵：從關隴集團掌握的隴右、關中、並州、河東抽取的軍戶，戰時自備甲仗與部分糧秣，番上之時自備裝具，大戰則由朝廷下募發文書，臨時徵集州郡丁役與雜役充軍。府兵之外有京師宿衛禁軍、邊鎮戍兵與各州郡團練，軍器由太府寺、弩坊與武器監一類官營作坊供給。指揮上，文帝不親征，詔發大軍後設行軍元帥與元帥長史，諸道各置行軍總管：並州總管李秀當井陘道攻定襄，幽州總管韋世康自北平道出，靈州總管楊素當靈武道，秦州總管衛叔寶當金城道，齊州總管李藥與潁州方面各當一路，王誼總節度，楊素為元帥長史。靈州是全軍樞紐，控黃河上游與河西走廊東口，向北可援朔州，向西可達涼州與西域商路，糧道、馬匹徵集與降眾安置皆以此為中心。突厥那邊，頗利可汗阿史那咄格控弦漠北與漠南大片草場，達頭可汗莫葛分掌西部與河西以北的部眾，兄弟為汗位與牧地互相攻伐；汗國無固定城郭，以牙帳為中樞，諸部散牧，編制分可汗直屬近衛騎、各部貝勒部眾與臨時徵發的丁騎，重輕騎混編，傾巢出動可達二十萬騎上下。隋朝敢於深入草原，靠的正是東西兩部的分裂與漠南內應者的存在。
countriesEn: The war that the Sui fought against the Turks from the nineteenth to the twentieth year of Kaihuang was between the Sui dynasty in the north and the Eastern Turkic Khaganate on the steppe, with a third party supplying the decisive pressure: the khans of the Turks destroying each other. On the Sui side, Emperor Wen, Yang Jian, was reigning in 599, the nineteenth year of Kaihuang, ten years after the conquest of Chen. The backbone of the army was the fubing militia: military households drawn from Longyou, Guanzhong, Bingzhou and Hedong under the control of the Guanlong group, who equipped themselves and in part supplied their own grain, and who, when the court issued a mustering order, were reinforced by the levies and the labouring men of the prefectures and commanderies. Beside the fubing stood the palace guard, the frontier garrisons and the local militia trains, while weapons came from the state workshops such as the Court of Imperial Household, the Crossbow Works and the Weapon Offices. Command was arranged without the emperor taking the field: once the host was ordered out, a xingjun yuanshuai and a zhangshi were named and each route had its own xingjun zongguan. Li Xiu, zongguan of Bingzhou, took the Jingxing route against Dingxiang; Wei Shikang of Youzhou marched out along the Beiping route; Yang Su of Lingzhou held the Lingwu route; Wei Shubao of Qinzhou took the Jincheng route; Li Yao of Qizhou and the men from Yingzhou took one route each; Wang Yi held overall command and Yang Su was his zhangshi. Lingzhou was the hinge of the whole army. It commanded the upper Yellow River and the eastern mouth of the Hexi Corridor, could reinforce Shuozhou to the north and reached Liangzhou and the western trade roads beyond; the supply line, the drawing of warhorses and the settlement of surrendered people all ran through it. On the Turkic side, Jieli Qaghan, Ashina Duge, held the northern steppe and the great pastures of the southern steppe, while Datou Qaghan, Moge, commanded the western part and the peoples north of the Hexi; the two brothers fought each other for the khanship and for grazing land. The steppe state had no fixed cities, its centre was the qaghan's camp, the tribes grazed where they pleased, and its organisation fell into the qaghan's own guard cavalry, the contingents of the various beiles, and the levies raised for the occasion, heavy and light riders mixed, with a host of some two hundred thousand horsemen when it moved in full. What allowed the Sui to strike deep into the steppe was precisely this split between the eastern and western halves, and the presence of a client inside the southern steppe.
people: 決策核心在長安，親臨前線的是楊素。隋文帝楊堅在開皇十九年已六十餘歲，不出宮城，只發詔、調兵、議糧，跨越數千里的戰役全交給行軍元帥與各道總管。楊素自太原起家，久鎮西邊，歷北周與隋的西北戰線；開皇十八年冬他率主力抵靈州，面對達頭可汗傾力來犯的二十萬騎，不硬碰而據險固守、蓄銳待疲，待敵解營稍懈才以夜襲掩襲其連營，斬首萬餘級，隨後乘勝追至磧口，奪其輜重無數。並州總管李秀所部在定襄方向受挫，敗還後被免職，反倒逼出主力西進、靈州集中的部署；幽州總管韋世康與秦州總管衛叔寶各當一路，負責牽制與追擊。真正改變戰局的是兵部尚書高熲與長孫晟一系的謀劃：高熲主張用離間把達頭與頗利之間的裂痕拉得更深，長孫晟早在開皇初年便證明，可以用少量使節與詐謀令草原諸部自相攻伐；高熲又設計把已在隋境內的突厥宗室啟民可汗扶上漠南汗位，既為內應，也為隋朝在北方留一個代言人。突厥那邊，達頭可汗莫葛並非全由隋軍殺死，他與頗利交攻，部眾怨恨其殘暴，開皇十九年兵敗眾潰，被部下所殺，單騎出走，餘眾十餘萬降隋。頗利可汗則靠和親與歲賜換得喘息，其母阿史那氏入長安朝見，隋文帝以宗女義成公主下嫁，另遣安修仁持金帛往撫，草原上的最高統治者一時稱臣於隋。
peopleEn: The decisions were made at Chang'an, but the fighting was led by Yang Su. Emperor Wen was over sixty by the nineteenth year of Kaihuang; he never left the palace, only issuing orders, shifting troops and discussing grain, and left expeditions of several thousand li entirely in the hands of the xingjun yuanshuai and the zongguan of each route. Yang Su, a native of Taiyuan, had long held the western frontier under Northern Zhou and Sui. In the winter of Kaihuang 18 he brought the main body to Lingzhou and faced the full host of some two hundred thousand horsemen that Datou Qaghan brought against him. He refused to meet them head on, entrenched on strong ground, stored up his strength and waited for the enemy to tire, and only when the enemy relaxed his camp did he strike at night against the chained encampments, taking more than ten thousand heads, and he pursued the broken enemy as far as Qikou, capturing an immense quantity of baggage. The force of Li Xiu, zongguan of Bingzhou, was checked in the Dingxiang direction with heavy losses, and Li Xiu was dismissed after the defeat, which was precisely what pushed the Sui to concentrate its main effort westward at Lingzhou; Wei Shikang of Youzhou and Wei Shubao of Qinzhou each took a route of their own, charged with containing the enemy and pursuing the defeated. What really bent the course of the war was the planning of Gao Zhi, zhangbu shangshu, and of the school around Changsun Sheng: Gao Zhi argued for widening the rift between Datou and Jieli, and Changsun Sheng had already shown as early as the first years of Kaihuang that a few envoys and a handful of false promises could set the steppe tribes fighting among themselves. Gao Zhi also arranged for Qimin Qaghan, a member of the Turkic ruling house who was already inside Sui territory, to be set up as kahan in the southern steppe, both as an internal agent and as a spokesman for the Sui in the north. On the Turkic side, Datou Qaghan, Moge, was not killed outright by Sui steel. He fought with Jieli, his followers resented his cruelty, and in 599 his host was beaten and dissolved; he was killed by his own men, rode out alone, and more than a hundred thousand of the survivors came over to the Sui. Jieli Qaghan bought himself breathing space by marriage and by the annual gifts that followed: his mother, a woman of the Ashina house, came to Chang'an to pay court, Emperor Wen married his clanswoman Princess Yicheng to him, and An Xiuren was sent with silk and treasure to reassure him, so that the highest ruler on the steppe for a time styled himself a subject of the Sui.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是羅馬標槍（Pilum）：半米長的投槍，槍幹中空，捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。它成形於公元前一百年前後的羅馬軍營，離開皇十九年的塞外戰場已超過六百九十九年，並不是此役現場的裝備。然而它指出的那個位置——用廉價而消耗的投射物去毀壞敵人的防具、逼敵退回陣後再攻——在開皇年間的塞外，兩邊都有人在做。突厥騎兵手持輕型標槍，在馬上拋擲，戳穿隋兵的大盾與薄甲，被刺穿的隋兵多半握著斷桿縮回槊陣後方重整隊形；隋朝這邊對應的投射物是弩，蹶張弩與床弩在陣前齊射，臂弩隨騎兵攜行，箭矢穿甲入盾之後同樣斷折，被射中的騎兵退回本陣重新整隊再衝。步兵的核心裝備是槊與戟，配大盾或腰盾列陣，陣前布拒馬槊與鹿角一類障礙器材，據《通典》記載是隋代所制、唐代沿用，用來擋住騎兵衝鋒；甲士著兩當甲、兜鍪，重裝只集中在少數人身上，多數兵卒只有一件皮甲或一片札甲。馬匹是真正的瓶頸：隋軍戰馬多來自河西與西域良馬，經涼州、甘肅一帶馬市交易取得，隨軍另備替馬，否則千里追擊撐不住。糧食以粟為主，配麥、豆、鹽、醋，乾餅與肉脯隨軍，牛車拖著糧車走，帳幕用氈張，士卒自攜十日之糧。突厥騎兵多著皮甲或鑲骨甲，角弓與筋弓射速快，骨鏃與鐵鏃兼用，配短矛、標槍與短刀，高鞍利於拈弓，紀律散漫而耐力驚人，能連續奔馳數日不食。羅馬標槍的真正價值不在殺傷幾人，而在它便宜、易補、折了再扔；這正是邊塞消耗戰的基本邏輯。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is a Roman pilum: a throwing pike about half a metre long with a hollow shaft, which snaps after it has been driven through a shield, so that the enemy can only drag himself back behind cover with half a spear still in him. It took shape in the Roman camp around 100 BC, more than six hundred and ninety-nine years before the field outside the wall in the nineteenth year of Kaihuang, and it was not the equipment on that field. Yet the place it marks out, using a cheap and consumed projectile to destroy the enemy's protection and drive him back behind his line to be formed up again, was occupied on both sides beyond the wall in those years. The Turkic horseman carried light javelins and threw them from the saddle, stabbing through the large shields and light armour of the Sui foot, and the Sui soldier so struck would usually fall back holding a broken shaft, shrinking behind the spear line to reform. The Sui counterpart of the throwing pike was the crossbow: the juzhang nu and the bed crossbow for massed shots in front of the line, the arm bow carried by the cavalry, and the bolts, having gone through armour or shield, broke there too, so that the rider who was hit withdrew to his own ranks, reformed and charged again. The core equipment of the infantry was the spear and the halberd, drawn up with large shields or waist shields; in front of the line stood obstacles such as the juma shuang and the lu jiao, which the Tongdian records as Sui inventions kept by the Tang, planted to stop a cavalry charge. The armoured men wore the liangdangjia and a helmet, and heavy protection was concentrated on a few men only, most soldiers having a leather coat or a single plate. Horses were the real bottleneck: most of the Sui warhorses were the fine animals of the Hexi and the western regions, bought at the horse markets of Liangzhou and Ganzhou, with remounts carried along, because a pursuit of a thousand li could not be sustained otherwise. The food was chiefly millet, with wheat, beans, salt and vinegar, dried cakes and dried meat travelling with the troops, ox carts dragging the grain wagons, tents made of felt, and ten days of rations carried by each man. The Turkic horseman usually wore leather or bone-studded armour, shot with bows of horn and sinew that were quick on the draw, used bone and iron arrowheads together, and carried short spears, javelins and a short knife, sitting on a high saddle that made the bow easier to handle; his discipline was loose but his endurance remarkable, for the riders could gallop for days without eating. The real value of the Roman pilum lay not in how many men it killed but in the fact that it was cheap, easy to replace, and could be thrown away after it broke, and that is the basic logic of a war of attrition on the frontier.
tactics: 隋軍的戰術核心有兩條：不要在開闊草原上跟二十萬騎兵硬拼正面，要把他們拖到沒有水草、沒有退路的樣子。開皇十八年冬，楊素抵靈州，兵力不足以與達頭傾力來犯的二十萬騎相抗，便據險而營，閉門不戰，蓄銳待疲；達頭屢次挑戰不得，解營稍懈，隋軍才以夜襲掩襲其連營，斬首萬餘級，乘勝追至磧口，奪其輜重無數，逼其不能重新結集。開皇十九年起，六路大軍齊進：井陘道、幽州道、靈武道、金城道、齊州與潁州方向同時壓上，把草原的縱深切成數段，主力則集中於靈州一路向西北深入。追擊是這場戰爭最吃力的部分：隋軍自靈州向北追過黃河，遠達鐵山、磧口一線，全程約四百至五百公里，穿越的是沒有城鎮、只有草場的河套與陰山南麓；塞外正月仍嚴寒多風，草原尚未返青，馬匹草料與飲水都要靠隨軍輸送，因此要靠沿途屯田糧倉與分遣驛騎維持，並以輕騎分隊以戰養戰。防守與掩護上，步兵結方陣，大盾與拒馬列於陣前，槊手斜舉長槊迎擊騎兵，弩手在陣後分層齊射，騎兵於兩翼展開，尋找突厥騎隊的側後；輜重車隊居中，牛車與護騎夾護糧車，前方一旦失利，糧車是必須先保住的東西。更高一層是外交與離間：高熲與長孫晟一系用使節往來、贈馬賜旗、散布部族猜忌，把達頭與頗利的內戰推到失控，再以啟民可汗在頗利軍中內應，使隋軍不必獨力承擔全部草原兵力。達頭正是在這樣的內外夾擊下崩潰：開皇十九年他兵敗眾潰，被部下所殺，餘眾十餘萬降隋。
tacticsEn: The Sui tactical plan rested on two points: do not meet two hundred thousand horsemen head on in the open steppe, but drag them until they have no water, no grass and nowhere to retreat. In the winter of Kaihuang 18 Yang Su reached Lingzhou with too few men to stand up to the full host of two hundred thousand horsemen that Datou Qaghan brought against him, so he entrenched on strong ground, kept his lines closed, stored up his strength and waited for the enemy to tire. Datou could not force a battle, so he relaxed his camp, and only then did the Sui strike at night against his chained encampments, taking more than ten thousand heads, pursue the broken enemy as far as Qikou, capture an immense quantity of baggage and prevent him from reforming. From 599 the six columns advanced together: the Jingxing, Beiping, Lingwu, Jincheng, Qizhou and Yingzhou routes pressed in at once, cutting the depth of the steppe into sections, while the main effort was concentrated on the Lingzhou route driving north-west. The pursuit was the hardest part of the campaign. The Sui rode north from Lingzhou, crossed the Yellow River and reached as far as the Tieshan and Qikou line, roughly four hundred to five hundred kilometres, through the Hetao and the southern foot of the Yin Mountains where there were no towns, only pasture. In the first month of the year the country beyond the wall was still bitterly cold and windy and the grass had not yet come up, so fodder and water for the horses had to travel with the army; the Sui therefore relied on the granaries of the frontier farms and on dispatch riders to keep going, with light cavalry squadrons living off the country as they moved. In defence and cover, the infantry closed into squares, with large shields and juma obstacles set in front, spearmen holding their long spears at an angle against the charge and crossbowmen firing in layered volleys from the rear, while the cavalry worked the flanks looking for the flanks of the Turkic horse-lines; the baggage train sat in the middle, ox carts and escort cavalry guarding the grain wagons, because if the front failed, the grain wagons were the things that had to be saved first. Above all of this sat diplomacy and division: Gao Zhi and the men around Changsun Sheng used embassies, gifts of horses and banners, and rumour to set the Turkic tribes against one another and to push the war between Datou and Jieli past breaking point, while Qimin Qaghan was used as an internal agent inside Jieli's camp, so that the Sui would not have to face the whole steppe host alone. Datou broke under exactly this pressure from two sides: in 599 his host was beaten and dissolved, he was killed by his own men, and more than a hundred thousand of his people came over to the Sui.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。《資治通鑑》卷一百八十五記開皇十八年十一月，隋文帝發兵三十萬擊突厥，分道六路出塞；三十萬是上限，實際投入戰鬥的只是其中一部，其餘是輜重、運輸與隨軍丁夫。《隋書·突厥傳》記達頭可汗率眾二十萬騎來犯靈州，兩軍在靈州、朔州一線反覆周旋，隋軍夜襲得手後斬首萬餘級，追擊階段奪其輜重不可勝計。開皇十九年達頭兵敗，眾十餘萬降隋，是《隋書·突厥傳》留下的最大一個數字，也是隋朝此後安置邊外部眾的主要來源。開皇二十年正月，隋朝再發兵三十萬出擊，諸將並出，頗利可汗大敗奔鐵山，五月遣使請和，其母阿史那氏至長安朝見，隋以宗女義成公主妻之；開皇二十一年頗利又寇定襄被大破，遣子入朝為質；開皇二十二年再追至沙鍊谷，頗利單騎遁走。距離上，靈州治所今寧夏靈武，鐵山一般指陰山南麓一線，自靈州至鐵山約四百至五百公里，正好是一支全騎兵大軍三至五日可及、而糧車需十日以上才能跟上的一段距離，這個速度差是隋軍能追上並拖垮突厥的關鍵。時間上，從開皇十八年冬發兵到開皇十九年達頭眾潰，前後不過三四個月；同年二月詔諸州修築長城，可見戰役的直接結果是改防線而非滅國。兵種比例上，一般估計隋唐府兵之中騎兵只佔兩成上下，故三十萬大軍是以步兵與徵發雜役為主體、以騎兵為打擊骨幹的混合部隊，這也是楊素在靈州必須靠夜襲與突進而非正面對撞的原因。傷亡數字各方記載互相矛盾，此處不列。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked run roughly as follows. The Zizhi Tongjian, volume 185, records that in the eleventh month of Kaihuang 18 the emperor raised three hundred thousand men against the Turks and sent them out in six columns; the three hundred thousand is a ceiling, and only part of it was ever engaged, the rest being baggage, transport and the labouring men who went with the army. The Biography of the Turks in the Book of Sui records Datou Qaghan coming against Lingzhou with some two hundred thousand horsemen, the two sides working against each other along the Lingzhou and Shuozhou lines, and the Sui night attack ending with more than ten thousand heads taken, the pursuit stage bringing back baggage that could not be counted. After Datou's defeat in 599, more than a hundred thousand came over to the Sui, the largest single figure the Book of Sui preserves for this campaign and the main source of the border population the dynasty later had to settle. In the first month of Kaihuang 20 the Sui raised three hundred thousand men again and sent the generals out on all sides; Jieli Qaghan was badly beaten and fled to Tieshan, and in the fifth month he sent envoys to ask for peace, his mother of the Ashina house coming to Chang'an to pay court, after which the Sui married him to its clanswoman Princess Yicheng; in 601 Jieli raided Dingxiang again and was badly beaten, and sent a son to the court as a hostage; in 602 he was pursued as far as the Shalian Valley and escaped on a single horse. In terms of distance, the seat of Lingzhou is modern Lingwu in Ningxia, and Tieshan generally denotes the southern foot of the Yin Mountains; the run from Lingzhou to Tieshan is roughly four hundred to five hundred kilometres, a stretch a fully mounted army could cover in three to five days and that a baggage train needed more than ten to keep up with. That gap in speed is the reason the Sui could catch the Turks and exhaust them. In time, from the mobilisation in the winter of Kaihuang 18 to the dispersal of Datou's host in 599, it was three or four months at most; in the second month of that same year the court ordered the prefectures to build and repair the Great Wall, which shows that the direct result of the campaign was a new line of defence and not the destruction of a state. On the balance of arms, scholarship generally puts mounted fubing at only around a fifth of the total, which means the three hundred thousand was in truth a mass of infantry and conscript labour with cavalry as its striking arm, and it is why Yang Su at Lingzhou had to win by night attack and penetration rather than by a head-on clash. Casualty figures conflict between the sources and are not listed here.
cause: 打起來的直接原因是突厥犯塞。開皇十八年冬，達頭部眾大舉南下，寇掠太原、朔州、靈州一線的城鎮與屯田，把塞內的邊防與軍屯拖進戰爭；同年夏天隋朝還要分兵救濟關東水旱與山東的飛蝗，兩邊負擔疊在一起，文帝楊堅不可能再聽任邊警年年響起。深一層原因是草原政權自身的分裂：頗利控弦漠北與漠南大片草場，達頭握有漠北西部與河西以北的部眾，兄弟二人為汗位與牧地互相攻伐，達頭的部眾同時怨恨其殘暴，隨時可能內變。隋朝看準的正是這個窗口。楊堅在開皇初年已用長孫晟的離間之策削弱突厥，開皇十八年北邊傳來達頭與頗利交攻的消息，朝廷便決定把打壓突厥提到與滅陳同等的位置，趁草原內鬥，以大軍直取其巢穴。第三個原因是國力已經到得夠：開皇九年高熲括戶，把州郡豪強隱庇的丁口重新登記入籍，租調收入與兵源因此增加；均田、租調與倉庫制度在開皇年間運作順暢，關中、隴右、河西的軍屯與漕運能夠把糧食一路送到靈州，府兵兵源也隨均田農戶上升而更充裕。第四個原因是戰略上的選擇：突厥的騎兵在開闊草原上無敵，一旦被引到河套、朔州之間的狹窄通道與寒冬的草場上，戰力就要打折；隋朝寧可用三十萬人押上來打一場，也不接受突厥年年南下逐鹿中原。第五個原因是外交上的配合：隋朝一面以宗女義成公主下嫁頗利可汗，用婚嫁與厚賚拖住漠北主力的注意力，一面把已受隋朝保護的啟民可汗作為內應的棋子，使任何一位可汗南下時都不敢把全部兵力帶走。
causeEn: The immediate reason for the fighting was a Turkic incursion. In the winter of Kaihuang 18 the people of Datou swept south in strength, raiding the towns and the military farms along the Taiyuan, Shuozhou and Lingzhou lines and dragging the frontier garrisons of the Sui into the war. Earlier in that same summer the Sui had still been sending relief troops to the floods in the east and the locusts in Shandong, and with the two burdens together Wen di could not afford to let the frontier alarms sound year after year. A deeper cause lay in the split inside the steppe polity itself. Jieli held the northern steppe and the great pastures of the southern steppe, Datou the western part and the peoples north of the Hexi; the two brothers fought each other for the khanship and for grazing land, and Datou's own followers resented his cruelty, so that defection was always possible. The Sui had noticed exactly that opening. Yang Jian had already used Changsun Sheng's policy of division to weaken the Turks in the first years of Kaihuang, and in 598 word came from the north that Datou and Jieli were at war, so the court decided to place the campaign against the Turks on the same level as the conquest of Chen and to strike at the heartland of the steppe while the Turks destroyed each other. A third cause was that the state had the strength to do it. In 589 Gao Zhi made a general survey of households and re-registered the people hidden by the great families of the prefectures, so that the state's grain revenue and its pool of soldiers grew; equal-field allocation, the grain-and-hemp system and the granaries worked smoothly through the Kaihuang years, and the military farms and river transport of Guanzhong, Longyou and the Hexi could move food all the way to Lingzhou, while the fubing levies grew with the expanding body of equal-field peasants. A fourth cause was a choice of method. Turkic cavalry was unbeatable on open grassland, but its strength fell away once it was drawn into the narrow ground between the Hetao and Shuozhou and onto winter pasture; the Sui was prepared to commit three hundred thousand men to a single battle rather than accept a situation in which the Turks came south every year. A fifth cause was the diplomatic cover: the Sui married its clanswoman Princess Yicheng to Jieli Qaghan, using the marriage and rich gifts to occupy the attention of the main northern host, while keeping Qimin Qaghan, already under Sui protection, as a pawn for an internal rising, so that no kahan dared bring every horseman south with him.
impact: 這一仗的直接後果，是草原權力格局的改變與隋朝邊防體制的定型。達頭兵敗身亡後，他與頗利之間的戰爭失去核心，漠北權力分成頗利與漠南受隋朝扶植的啟民兩塊，突厥內部再沒有一個能服眾的可汗。開皇二十年頗利可汗趁隋朝大勝之餘再度大舉南下，隋軍再出，頗利大敗，僅以身免；同年五月請和、義成公主下嫁，次年遣子入朝為質，開皇二十二年又追至沙鍊谷，漠南的游牧政權退到陰山以北，隋朝邊境自此安定近二十年，直到隋末天下大亂、突厥再度南下。對隋朝本身，這場戰爭帶來兩樣東西。第一樣是防線：開皇十九年二月詔諸州修築長城，塞內外築城置兵、積粟轉運，河套與陰山南麓從此成為王朝的邊界與軍屯地帶，隋朝由以攻為守轉為以守為攻。第二樣是代價：達頭部眾十餘萬降隋，連同陸續內附的部眾，國家在邊疆背上了安置、給種、編戶與供糧的負擔；開皇末年府兵調發日密，隋朝連續三次大舉征高句麗，耗空國力，導致亂事蜂起、隋室傾覆——北邊省下的開支，二十年後終究從南邊吐了出來。對草原而言，這一場戰爭確立了中原王朝與北方游牧政權互有輸贏的基本格局，也為唐太宗貞觀四年（630）的定襄之戰鋪了路：啟民可汗在漠南既是唐軍的耳目，也是東突厥內部分裂的明證，李靖的十萬騎得以直搗牙帳。
impactEn: The immediate consequences of the war were a rearrangement of power on the steppe and the fixing of the Sui frontier system. With Datou beaten and killed, the war between him and Jieli lost its pivot, and authority in the steppe split into Jieli in the north and the Sui-backed Qimin in the south, so that there was no longer a kahan whom the steppe could accept. In 600 Jieli Qaghan swept south in force once more, taking advantage of the Sui's recent victory, and the Sui moved out to meet him; Jieli was badly beaten and escaped with nothing but his life. In the fifth month he asked for peace, Princess Yicheng was married to him, a son was sent to the court as a hostage the following year, and in 602 he was pursued as far as the Shalian Valley; the nomadic power of the southern steppe withdrew north of the Yin Mountains, and the Sui frontier enjoyed close to twenty years of quiet, until the collapse of the Sui and the renewed descent of the Turks. The Sui itself gained two things from this war. The first was a frontier. In the second month of Kaihuang 19 the prefectures were ordered to build and repair the Great Wall, to build forts and station troops inside and outside the frontier and to accumulate grain for transport; the Hetao and the southern foot of the Yin Mountains became the dynasty's border and its farm belt, and the Sui shifted from attacking in defence to holding in defence. The second was the cost. More than a hundred thousand of Datou's people came over, and with the tribes that followed, the state took on the burden of settling them, giving them stock, registering them as households and feeding them; as the fubing levies were called out ever more densely near the end of Kaihuang, the Sui spent itself on three great campaigns against Goguryeo, emptied the treasury, and was eaten by disorder until the dynasty fell: the money saved in the north was paid back with interest in the south twenty years later. For the steppe, the campaign set the basic pattern of the exchanges between the agricultural state and the nomadic powers. It also paved the way for the Dingxiang campaign of 630 under Taizong of Tang: Qimin Qaghan in the southern steppe was both an ear for the Tang army and plain proof that the Eastern Turks were divided, and Li Jing's hundred thousand riders could go straight for the qaghan's tent.
result: 隋朝在開皇十八年至二十年取得了乾淨的勝利。達頭可汗的牙帳被夜襲打散，大軍在追擊中崩潰，他本人被部下所殺，單騎遁走，餘眾十餘萬降隋；靈州與朔州一線的塞外通道被打開，隋朝的追擊一直推進到鐵山、磧口一線，達頭部眾的抵抗意志在缺草、缺水、缺補給的草原上瓦解。隋朝隨即在開皇十九年二月詔諸州修築長城，塞內外築城置兵、積粟轉運，把戰役的成果變成可以長期使用的邊防工程：靈州、朔州一線成為屯田與轉運的基地，降眾被編入州縣，給牛羊令其耕牧，隋朝在漠南第一次擁有了穩定的後方基地。但這一場勝仗並不等於草原平定。頗利可汗仍在漠北稱雄，開皇二十年仍能率眾大舉南下；直到和親、質子與沙鍊谷一役之後，東突厥的分裂才告一段落，隋朝邊境又安定了二十餘年。從兵制與戰爭的觀點看，這場戰役也留下了一套可複用的經驗：以方陣、大盾與長槊硬扛騎兵衝鋒，用弩的齊射把衝鋒打散，再以兩翼騎兵反擊側後；用離間與內應替自己分擔敵人的兵力；最重要的是不靠一場血戰定勝負，而靠把敵人拖到沒有補給的遠處，靠兵源與糧道的持續供應撐到最後。卡面那件羅馬標槍不在此役現場，但它那句話在靈州到鐵山的四五百公里裡一點都沒錯：一件便宜的投槍折了可以再扔，一把大盾破了可以再補，而戰爭的勝負從來取決於背後還有多少人、還有多少糧。
resultEn: The Sui won cleanly between the eighteenth and the twentieth year of Kaihuang. The camp of Datou Qaghan was broken by a night attack, the host collapsed during the pursuit, he himself was killed by his own men, rode out alone, and more than a hundred thousand of his people came over to the Sui. The corridor outside the wall between Lingzhou and Shuozhou was opened, the pursuit ran as far as the Tieshan and Qikou line, and the will to resist broke down in a steppe with no grass, no water and no supply. The Sui then turned the victory into something permanent: in the second month of Kaihuang 19 the prefectures were ordered to build and repair the Great Wall, to build forts and station troops inside and outside the frontier and to accumulate grain for transport, so that the Lingzhou and Shuozhou line became a base for farms and for the transport of supplies, and the surrendered people were enrolled in the prefectures, given cattle and sheep and set to plough and graze. For the first time the Sui held a stable base in the southern steppe. But the victory was not pacification. Jieli Qaghan was still master in the northern steppe and could still bring a great host south in 600; it was only after the marriage, the hostage and the battle in the Shalian Valley that the fragmentation of the Eastern Turks was settled and the frontier enjoyed more than twenty years of quiet. From the point of view of military systems and of warfare, the campaign also left behind a set of reusable lessons: meet the cavalry charge with a square, large shields and long spears; break the charge with massed crossbow fire; then send your own cavalry around the flanks. Use division and internal agents to take part of the enemy's strength off him. And above all, do not try to settle the matter in one battle, but drag the enemy out to where he cannot be supplied and hold on with replacements and grain until the end. The Roman pilum on the card was not on that field, but its sentence was exactly right across the four or five hundred kilometres from Lingzhou to Tieshan: a cheap throwing pike that breaks can be thrown away again, a large shield that is split can be replaced, and what decides a war has never been the weapon in the front rank but how many men and how much grain are still behind you.
